article.articleHeadline: Health: Uganda, WHO agree on coordinated Ebola response as T
article.articleSummary: Uganda confirmed two imported Ebola Bundibugyo Virus Disease cases from eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, with one death and one recovery. WHO Director-General Tedros said the Uganda situation remains stable. Uganda and WHO agreed to strengthen coordination and public communication on the outbreak. Uganda has fully activated response systems, deploying rapid response teams across priority districts and sharpening surveillance at border points and health facilities. The country maintained transparency and information-sharing with international partners in line with the International Health Regulations. The briefing in Geneva on May 22 focused on the Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC and Uganda, noting separate epidemiological contexts. Uganda emphasised the need for coordinated communication among governments, international agencies, and partners to avoid panic and maintain public confidence during the response.

article.articleHeadline: Risicovol en zwaar: Nederlandse helpt bij bestrijding ebola in Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Risky and arduous: a Dutch aid worker helps combat Ebola in the Congo
article.articleSummary: As of 23 May 2026, Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo are being addressed by Doctors Without Borders (MSF). Dutch aid worker Anna Simon travels to the DRC to assist in the response. There have been hundreds of Ebola infections reported, with fears that many more may be infected. Simon explains how the Ebola response works on the ground, offering a glimpse into frontline efforts during a dangerous and emotionally heavy operation. The article underscores the human toll on responders and the risks involved in outbreak control. It also highlights ongoing international aid involvement aimed at containing the disease and protecting communities amid challenging conditions in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

triage.headline_ja: 危険で困難な作業：オランダの支援者がコンゴでのエボラ対策を支援
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で3項目該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際的対応）。WPROスクリーニング基準でも複数該当（重症度、流行しやすさ、管理可能性）。DRCでのエボラアウトブレイクは確認済みで、国際的支援が展開中。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでのエボラアウトブレイク対応の報道。オランダの支援者が関与しているため Netherlands も発生地域に含まれているが、実際のアウトブレイク地域はDRCのみ。対象国リストにはDRCが含まれているため verified_locations に追加。数百件のエボラ感染が報告されており、MSFなどの国際機関が対応に当たっている。フルRRA進行推奨。

article.articleHeadline: В Уганде число заразившихся лихорадкой Эбола возросло до пяти
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Uganda, the number of people infected with Ebola fever has risen to five.
article.articleSummary: Uganda reports Ebola virus disease infections rising to five confirmed cases as of May 23, 2026. Three new cases were confirmed, bringing the total to five. The new infections include two individuals— a driver and a healthcare worker— who had contact with the first infected person, and a citizen of the Democratic Republic of the Congo who was in Uganda. The Uganda Ministry of Health announced the figures on social media via Report. No deaths are reported in the article. The cases indicate ongoing person-to-person transmission linked to the initial infection, and authorities say surveillance and contact tracing are continuing to contain the outbreak in the country.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダでエボラ熱の感染者数が5人に増加
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で3項目該当（異常性、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）。WPROスクリーニング基準で4項目該当（異常性、ヒト-ヒト感染の可能性、管理能力の懸念、国境を越えた感染例）。エボラウイルス病は高致死率の感染症であり、複数国での確認と進行中の感染拡大リスクがあるため、フルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーではウガンダでの確認症例5例とDRCからの入国者を含む。進行中のヒト-ヒト感染（運転手、医療従事者が初発患者との接触で感染）が確認されており、エボラウイルス病の高い病原性と感染力を考慮すると、国際的な懸念が高い。死亡例は記事では報告されていないが、潜伏期間中の症例や重症化リスクがある。

article.articleHeadline: Trois nouveaux cas du virus Ebola confirmés en Ouganda
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Three new cases of the Ebola virus confirmed in Uganda.
article.articleSummary: Three new Ebola cases confirmed in Uganda, bringing total in the country to five. Uganda had previously announced Ebola on May 15 after two cases, one of whom died. The three new cases are: a Ugandan driver who transported the first confirmed patient within Uganda; a health-care worker infected while treating him; and a Congolese woman who arrived in Uganda by air. All contacts linked to the confirmed cases have been identified and are under surveillance. Uganda has suspended all public transport to the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The WHO has declared an international health emergency for the Congo outbreak, which reports around 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths. There is no licensed vaccine or approved treatment for the Bundibugyo Ebola strain; containment relies on barrier precautions and rapid case detection.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダでエボラウイルスの新たな3例が確認
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目中3項目に該当。エボラウイルスの国際的拡大、WHO国際保健緊急事態宣言、死亡事例を含む重症例が複数確認されており、フルRRA実施が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため除外。ただしDRCはリスト内であり、記事サマリーで「WHO has declared an international health emergency for the Congo outbreak」と明記されており、DRCが主要な発生地として確認される。ウガンダへの流出例も報告されているが、DRCが疫学的中心。

article.articleHeadline: Campinas (SP): Brasileiro cria microscópio barato para diagnóstico de malária na Nigéria
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Campinas (SP): Brazilian creates cheap microscope for malaria diagnosis in Nigeria.
article.articleSummary: Campinas (SP), Brazil-based researchers developed a low-cost malaria diagnostic microscope for Nigeria’s Yobe state. The cell-phone–connected device costs about $85 and has been distributed as 30 units to regional hospitals. It is locally assembled in under an hour from online parts, including a 12‑MP USB camera and 3D-printed components, with power supplied by the connected smartphone. Built on open hardware, the design provides free access to plans and materials, fostering local autonomy. The microscope targets microscopic blood analysis—the WHO standard for malaria diagnosis—and aims to speed diagnosis and treatment where rapid tests lack precision. The platform may also support other tests, such as Pap smear–based cervical cancer screening, and enable digital epidemiology databases. Validation in Nigeria is ongoing, adapting the OpenFlexure project; early results show red blood cells and malaria parasites. Expansion and training are planned.

triage.headline_ja: カンピーナス（SP）：ブラジル人がナイジェリアでのマラリア診断用の低価格顕微鏡を開発

article.articleHeadline: الصحة العالمية: معدل وفيات فيروس الإيبولا 50% وتطوير لقاحات لسلالة بونديبوجيو
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization: Ebola virus case fatality rate is 50% and development of vaccines for the Bundibugyo strain.
article.articleSummary: May 23, 2026 — The World Health Organization updated on Ebola virus disease caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), noting that early supportive care—hydration and symptom management—remains foundational to saving lives, with case fatality around 50% and historically up to 90% in past outbreaks. Ebola results from three main strains in the genus Orthoebolavirus: Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV), Sudan virus (SUDV), and Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). Vaccines and antibody therapies have been developed for EBOV, but no licensed vaccines or treatments exist yet for SUDV or BDBV. WHO is pursuing vaccines for BDBV, though development may take six to nine months. The virus first emerged in 1976 in South Sudan and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Ongoing efforts emphasize rapid supportive care and continued research into strain-specific vaccines.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関: エボラウイルスの致死率は50%でありブンディブギオ株のワクチン開発が進行中

article.articleHeadline: أوغندا تسجل 3 إصابات جديدة بـ "إيبولا" والصحة العالمية ترفع درجة الخطر
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Uganda records 3 new Ebola cases, and the World Health Organization raises the risk level.
article.articleSummary: As of May 23, 2026, Uganda reports three new laboratory-confirmed cases of deadly Ebola virus disease, signaling accelerated transmission to a country bordering the Democratic Republic of Congo, the outbreak’s main hotspot. The World Health Organization has raised the risk level in response to this developing situation. The report emphasizes cross-border movement toward Uganda as part of the ongoing Ebola outbreak centered in the DRC, illustrating the geographic reach of the current transmission and signaling that the outbreak is no longer confined to a single country. The information provided is limited to confirmation status of the cases and the location context; no additional clinical details are included in the brief.

triage.notes: 発生地域にUgandaが含まれているが、記事サマリーの主題はDRCでの継続的な流行と、それがウガンダへの国境越境移動による拡大を示すもの。対象国リストにUgandaが含まれていないため、verified_locationsはDRCのみ。ただし、DRCが対象国であり、エボラの国際的拡大を示す重要なシグナルであるため、PICKUP判定は確定。

article.articleHeadline: أوغندا تؤكد 3 إصابات جديدة بفيروس إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Uganda confirms 3 new Ebola virus infections.
article.articleSummary: As of May 23, 2026, Uganda confirms three new Ebola virus infections, bringing the total number of confirmed cases in the country to five. The Ministry of Health said the three newly identified cases are: a Ugandan driver who transported a person who was the first confirmed case in Uganda; a health-care worker who contracted Ebola while caring for that patient; and a woman from Congo. The update indicates ongoing transmission linked to the initial case, with infections occurring among individuals with direct exposure to the patient or involved in his care. The report does not provide further clinical details, laboratory confirmation specifics, or information on symptoms, exposure timelines, or potential travel history beyond the described contacts. The situation underscores continued monitoring and contact tracing as authorities respond to the cluster.

article.articleHeadline: Épidémie d'Ebola: la communauté scientifique se mobilise et prépare la riposte sanitaire
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Outbreak: The Scientific Community Mobilizes and Prepares the Public Health Response.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak, Bundibugyo variant, in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, triggers a global scientific response. On May 22, 2026, the WHO-supported Consortium for Filovirus Research held a first-of-its-kind virtual meeting to map current knowledge and tools for outbreak response. Plans call for rapid deployment of Ebola treatment centers in eastern DRC and exploration of two promising therapeutic avenues: monoclonal antibodies (one product developed by a U.S. laboratory with U.S. government funding) and broad-spectrum antivirals such as remdesivir (Gilead). A rigorous, consensual clinical trial protocol will take several weeks to finalize. Vaccine development against the Bundibugyo strain lags behind. More than 1,300 participants joined the session, underscoring international interest; organizers stress ensuring field realities, including a viable economic model to ensure future treatments and vaccines are available in adequate quantities at affordable prices.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱流行：科学界が動員され公衆衛生対応を準備
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）の流行であり、深刻な公衆衛生影響、国際的な科学的動員、国際的な治療開発・展開計画により、国際保健上の懸念事項である。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはコンゴ民主共和国東部でのエボラ流行を主題としており、DRCが確実な発生地である。アメリカは治療薬開発国として言及されているが、疾病の実発生地ではないため verified_locations から除外。DRCは対象国リストに含まれているため適切にピックアップされた。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: WHO stuft Risiko im Kongo als "sehr hoch" ein
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: WHO classifies the risk in the Congo as "very high".
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has prompted WHO to raise risk from high to very high, with regional risk high. Surge in suspected cases, undetected transmission chains, and spread into border areas amid conflict drive the assessment. Nearly 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths have been reported; actual numbers are likely higher due to underreporting and a backlog in lab investigations. Despite the heightened local risk, WHO says the global risk remains low because Ebola spreads mainly through close contact with bodily fluids and previous cases have been largely regional. The EU Commission is providing €15 million to Congo and Uganda for outbreak response, preparedness, and prevention. The EU and UNICEF are organizing a humanitarian air bridge, with a first flight from Liège planned next Monday delivering about 100 tonnes of relief goods to eastern Congo, including medicines, protective gear, and equipment for medical teams.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ：WHOがコンゴでのリスクを「非常に高い」と分類
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ以上該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限のリスク）、WPRO基準も複数該当（重症度、流行しやすさ、管理可能性）。DRCでのエボラ発生、WHOによる重大警告、および国際的対応が進行中であり、シグナルとして識別される。
